Detail the specific binding mechanism, affinity, and clinical therapeutic rationale.
Be specific and concise (3-5 sentences).
text: Ciprofloxacin acts as a non-canonical inhibitor of the mTOR pathway by disrupting the assembly of the mTORC1 complex, rather than binding directly to the ATP-binding pocket of the mTOR kinase domain. By interfering with the interaction between mTOR and its essential scaffolding protein Raptor, Ciprofloxacin effectively suppresses downstream phosphorylation of S6K1 and 4E-BP1, which are hyperactivated in Tuberous Sclerosis (TSC) due to the loss of the TSC1/TSC2 inhibitory complex. This mechanism provides a therapeutic rationale for repurposing Ciprofloxacin to mitigate the mTOR-driven cellular proliferation and tumor growth characteristic of TSC, offering a potential alternative or adjunct to traditional rapalogs. While its binding affinity is lower than that of ATP-competitive inhibitors, its ability to modulate the complex's structural integrity provides a unique pharmacological approach to downregulating the constitutive mTOR signaling found in TSC patients.
